questions.question: Which of the following is NOT shown as an actor in the Mentcare system use‑case diagram?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The diagram (Figure 4.15, p. 25) lists Nurse, Doctor and Medical receptionist as actors; an Administrator does not appear.

questions.question: Why does the text suggest adding extra information (tables or graphical models) to natural‑language requirements?

options.B: To illustrate how computations proceed, state changes, and user interactions
options.C: To eliminate the need for testing
options.D: To reduce the amount of documentation required

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Page 24 explains that extra information can show computation flow, system‑state changes, and interaction sequences.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] The text states that a teacher moderates the uploaded photos.

questions.question: How are use cases related to the Unified Modeling Language (UML) according to the passage?

options.B: They are a fundamental feature of UML.
options.C: They replace class diagrams in UML.
options.D: They are only used in data‑flow diagrams.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] Page 25 says use cases “have now become a fundamental feature of the Unified Modeling Language (UML).”

questions.question: What specific benefit does the tabular specification of computation (Figure 4.14, p. 24) provide over plain text?

options.A: It defines the system’s color palette.
options.B: It gives a precise sequencing of computational steps.
options.C: It lists hardware component part numbers.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] The text notes that tables can “show how computations proceed,” implying precise sequencing.

questions.question: According to the Mentcare use‑case diagram, which activity is most likely performed by the Medical receptionist?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] In the picture text (p. 25) “Generate report” appears alongside “Medical receptionist personal info,” indicating that generating reports is a receptionist task.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of using use cases to describe interactions between users and a system?

options.C: To capture functional requirements from the user’s viewpoint

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] The passage (p. 25) describes use cases as “a way of describing interactions between users and a system,” i.e., capturing functional requirements.

questions.question: Compared with plain‑text requirements, graphical models such as use‑case diagrams primarily improve what aspect of requirement communication?
questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Easy] Page 24 emphasizes that graphical models “show how users interact with the system,” enhancing visual communication.

questions.question: The citation of Dijkstra’s 1972 article (p. 36) serves what purpose in the context of the discussion on requirements?

options.A: It introduces the concept of use cases.
options.B: It critiques programming style unrelated to requirements.
options.C: It provides historical background on thoughtful software engineering, supporting the need for clear specifications.
options.D: It describes the syntax of UML use‑case diagrams.

questions.explanation: [Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Although the passage does not detail the article, its inclusion alongside requirement‑specification material suggests it offers a historical perspective on disciplined software development, reinforcing the argument for precise requirements.
